captures.notes: Every byte is US-ASCII; there is not one binary field, not one length field, and not one fixed-width field in the whole datagram. Field extents are determined ONLY by the delimiters 0x3a (colon), 0x20 (OWS) and 0d0a. Values I chose because the capture needed a legal one: USER-AGENT product tokens, and MX=3. HOST is mandatory and is fixed by the spec to the SSDP group; on IPv6 it would read [FF02::C]:1900 instead. Header ORDER here (HOST, MAN, MX, ST, USER-AGENT) is the conventional Windows ordering but is NOT normative — any permutation is the same message.

captures.notes: Legal values I chose rather than captured: the UUID (4d696e69-444c-164e-9d41-b827eb2f1c3a — version nibble 1, variant nibble 9, so a well-formed RFC 4122 v1 UUID), the LOCATION host/port, the SERVER product token, and the DATE. DATE is optional in UPnP; I included it because it is the field that breaks the converter set. EXT is written in its canonical no-value form 'EXT:' — many real stacks emit 'EXT: ' with a trailing space, which is the SAME message but 316 bytes. A root device answering ssdp:all sends N SEPARATE datagrams like this one (rootdevice, uuid:<id>, and one per embedded device/service type), each differing only in ST/USN.

statefulness: See the `statefulness` analysis field — full text supplied there.

gaps.what: No delimiter-terminated field kind. Every field extent in both captures is set by a delimiter, never by a width or a length prefix.
gaps.why: Response bytes 17..43 are `CACHE-CONTROL: max-age=1800`. The name ends at the 0x3a at offset 30, the value ends at the 0d0a at offset 44. Nothing in the datagram says 13 or 12. Every width-bearing construct in §3 — scalars, `repeat:n`, `skip:n`, `pad:{to}`, `each:<count>` — requires a statically known or already-captured length, and SSDP has no length field anywhere in its 315 bytes. The showpiece two-pass `len(group:X)` back-patcher is 100% unused by this protocol.
gaps.proposedFix: { "until": "0d0a", "as": "line", "consume": true, "max": 2048 }  // and { "until": "3a", "as": "name" }. Decode: scan forward to the delimiter, capture the span before it, optionally consume it. Encode: emit the value then the delimiter, and validate at document-validate time that the value cannot contain the delimiter. `max` keeps the packet bound computable in the spirit of §4's loop bound.

gaps.what: No repeat-until-sentinel. The number of headers is unknown, unbounded, and stated nowhere in the bytes.
gaps.why: The request carries 5 headers, the response 9. The only signal that the header section has ended is the empty line — 0d0a at 140 in the request, 0d0a at 313 in the response. §3's `each` takes either a count expression (`capture.byteCount / 2`) or a list to iterate; there is no count to give it, and the list does not exist until after parsing. So the header section cannot be iterated at all.
gaps.proposedFix: { "repeatUntil": { "peek": "0d0a" }, "max": 64, "as": "headers", "fields": [ … ] }  // `peek` tests without consuming; the loop exits on the blank line, which is then consumed by an explicit { "expect": "0d0a" }. `max` is a constant <= 256, mirroring §4's declared-cycle rule so the bound stays static.

gaps.what: No unordered key/value field kind. Header order is not significant in SSDP, but a v0 field list is strictly positional.
gaps.why: My response emits CACHE-CONTROL, DATE, EXT, LOCATION, SERVER, ST, USN, BOOTID, CONFIGID. A different device emits exactly the same message as ST, USN, LOCATION, SERVER, CACHE-CONTROL — and my positional parse reads `upnp:rootdevice` (offset 189) into the field named cacheControl. Both are valid SSDP. The grammar cannot express 'a set of named items in any order', so byte-order-dependent parsing is the only option and it is wrong for the protocol.
gaps.proposedFix: { "headers": { "kind": "httpHeaders", "terminator": "0d0a0d0a", "nameFold": "lower", "keepRaw": true, "as": "hdrs" } }  // one field kind that owns the whole header section, emits a Map, and stores per-entry { rawName, ows, value, index } so re-encode is verbatim.

gaps.what: ProtoValue has no Map kind, so parsed headers have nowhere to live and no way to be addressed.
gaps.why: §6 defines ProtoValue as Bytes | Int | Text | List. Even given the field kind above, `capture.hdrs['location']` is not expressible — a List of pairs cannot be indexed by name (there is no record type and `each … as:"r"` binds a scalar). Downstream, `emits` needs `capture.hdrs.usn` and `effects` needs `capture.hdrs.cacheControl`; both are unreachable.
gaps.proposedFix: Add Map to ProtoValue and two converters: `key(name)` (Map -> Text, case-folded lookup, first match) and `all(name)` (Map -> List, for repeated headers). Then `capture.hdrs | key('location')`. Type-checkable at validate time like every other converter, so §6's validate-time guarantee survives.

gaps.what: No Int <-> decimal-ASCII converter. Every number in this protocol is decimal text and the closed converter set cannot produce or consume it.
gaps.why: Request byte 75 is 0x33, the decimal digit 3, for MX. Response bytes 40..43 are `1800`, 9..11 are `200`, 288 is `1` (BOOTID), 310 is `1` (CONFIGID), and 120..124 inside LOCATION are the port `49152`. §6's encode group is hex/base64/mac/ip/dnsName; the numeric group is binary widths (u16be etc.); `hexint` gives hex. Nothing maps Int 3 -> the byte 0x33 or the byte 0x33 -> Int 3. Consequence: every numeric input must be declared `type: text`, which kills range validation (MX must be 1..5), kills arithmetic (the listen window is mx*1000), and makes `capture.statusCode == 200` a type error.
gaps.proposedFix: Add to the numeric group: `decimal` (Int -> Text, optional width/zero-pad arg: `decimal(2,'0')` for the day field of DATE) and `undecimal` (Text -> Int, strict, rejects leading +/space/empty). Then `inputs.mx | decimal | ascii` and `capture.statusCode | undecimal == 200`. Smallest possible fix and it unblocks every text protocol, not just this one.

gaps.what: No RFC 1123 / IMF-fixdate converter, so the DATE header cannot be generated.
gaps.why: Response bytes 52..80 are `Sun, 09 Aug 2026 12:00:00 GMT` — 29 bytes with an English day abbreviation, an English month abbreviation, a zero-padded day, and a literal GMT. §6's time group offers epochSeconds, epochMillis, ntpTimestamp, iso8601. `now.utc | iso8601` yields `2026-08-09T12:00:00Z` — wrong length, wrong content, wrong every byte. The only in-spec workaround is to accept the whole 29 bytes as an opaque text input, at which point the grammar validates nothing.
gaps.proposedFix: Add `httpDate` (Instant -> Text, IMF-fixdate, always GMT, C-locale names) and `unhttpDate` (Text -> Instant, accepting the two obsolete RFC 850 / asctime forms on decode per RFC 7231 but emitting only IMF-fixdate). Then `{ "value": "now.utc | httpDate | ascii" }`. Note the decode direction is deliberately more permissive than encode — the converter table should be allowed to declare that asymmetry.

gaps.what: The udp layer has no multicast configuration. §2 describes it as 'engine sets ports + broadcast flag', and broadcast is not multicast.
gaps.why: This datagram must go to 239.255.255.250:1900 with IP_MULTICAST_TTL=2 (UPnP mandates TTL 2 by default), IP_MULTICAST_IF pinned to a chosen adapter (a multihomed host with a VPN will otherwise send it out the wrong interface and discover nothing), and loopback typically disabled. To receive NOTIFY announcements the socket must additionally bind port 1900 with SO_REUSEADDR and issue IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP for the group. `adapter.*` exposes ip/mac/broadcast/prefix/gateway — a broadcast address, which is the wrong mechanism. Every udp-layer key in my encode document is invented because v0 specifies none.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify the udp layer schema and add a multicast block: { "kind":"udp", "dst":{"ip":"239.255.255.250","port":1900}, "bind":{"port":0}, "multicast":{ "join":true, "group":"239.255.255.250", "ttl":2, "iface":"adapter.ip", "loopback":false, "reuseAddr":true } }. Also needed for mDNS, LLMNR, WS-Discovery and Bonjour, so it generalises well beyond SSDP.

gaps.what: No `dest.*` expression path, so the HOST header duplicates the transport destination with nothing keeping them in sync.
gaps.why: Request bytes 27..46 spell `239.255.255.250:1900` as a const. The udp layer separately targets the same address. HTTP requires HOST to name the destination, and for IPv6 SSDP it must read `[FF02::C]:1900` (link-local) or `[FF05::C]:1900` (site-local) — different bytes AND different bracket syntax. Retarget the transport and these 20 bytes stay silently, wrongly the same.
gaps.proposedFix: Expose `dest.ip`, `dest.port`, and `dest.hostport` (already bracket-correct for IPv6) as expression paths resolved from the enclosing transport layer, then write { "value": "dest.hostport | ascii" }. One derived value, no duplication, correct across address families.

gaps.what: `broadcast` correlation yields a list, but there is no per-item scope — so N discovered devices cannot become N facts.
gaps.why: This is the entire point of M-SEARCH. One request produces many unicast replies over the MX window, from many devices, and a single root device legitimately sends several non-duplicate replies to `ssdp:all` (one for upnp:rootdevice as captured, one for uuid:<id>, one per embedded device and service type), differing only in ST (bytes 189..203) and USN (211..268). §4 says broadcast 'yields a list'; §1 says `emits` is 'capture -> DeviceFact bindings', singular, and `capture.*` is scalar-shaped throughout §6. There is no `capture[i]`, no iteration on emitFact, and no grouping key.
gaps.proposedFix: { "id":"record", "kind":"emitFact", "forEach":"capture.responses", "as":"r", "identity":"r.hdrs | key('usn') | split('::') | index(0)", "groupBy":"identity", "facts": { "dev.upnp.location":"r.hdrs | key('location')", "dev.upnp.server":"r.hdrs | key('server')" } }  // plus the `index(n)` list converter, which §6 also lacks.

gaps.what: `token` correlation is unsound for SSDP: the obvious token deliberately does not echo.
gaps.why: The natural correlator is the ST echo. But request bytes 82..89 are `ssdp:all` while response bytes 189..203 are `upnp:rootdevice` — the responder substitutes its own target and MUST do so. A token correlator configured on ST silently drops every reply to the most common search there is. Correlation is really (ephemeral source port) + (MX time window) + (a conditional ST predicate).
gaps.proposedFix: { "correlate": { "kind":"predicate", "when": "inputs.searchTarget == 'ssdp:all' || capture.hdrs | key('st') == inputs.searchTarget", "collect": "all", "windowMs": "inputs.mx | undecimal * 1000 + 500" } }  // generalises `token` (which is just the equality case) rather than adding a fourth correlation kind.

gaps.what: `effects.ttl` is a literal duration; SSDP's fact lifetime is declared by the device in the response body.
gaps.why: Response bytes 32..43 are `max-age=1800`: the device is asserting 'presume me present for 1800 seconds and then stop'. §5 shows `"ttl": "PT30S"` — a constant. A constant TTL either expires live devices early or, far worse, keeps dead devices in the graph indefinitely. Soft-state expiry IS SSDP; a hardcoded TTL is not an approximation of it, it is a different protocol.
gaps.proposedFix: Allow ttl to be an expression and add one converter: { "effects": { "presume": {...}, "confidence":"likely", "ttl": "capture.hdrs | key('cacheControl') | regex('max-age=(\\d+)',1) | undecimal | seconds" } }, where `seconds` is Int -> Duration in the time group. `regex` already exists in the text group.

gaps.what: No epoch/generation invalidation primitive. BOOTID is the real state variable and §5 has no concept for it.
gaps.why: Response bytes 271..288 are `BOOTID.UPNP.ORG: 1`. When a device reboots or changes IP it increments this, and that increment invalidates EVERY cached fact about the device — location, description, service list, live GENA subscriptions. CONFIGID.UPNP.ORG (bytes 291..310) increments separately when the description document changes, invalidating the cached XML but not the identity. §5's known-gaps list mentions sequence numbers only as replay protection; this is not replay protection, it is a scope-wide cache generation.
gaps.proposedFix: "epochs": [ { "name":"bootId", "value":"capture.hdrs | key('bootId') | undecimal", "scope":"device", "onChange":"invalidateScope" }, { "name":"configId", "value":"capture.hdrs | key('configId') | undecimal", "scope":"message:describe", "onChange":"invalidateScope" } ]  // monotonic; a decrease means a different device reusing the UUID and should raise, not silently accept.

gaps.what: No `invalidatedBy` — §5 can express positive confirmation of a presumption but not retraction.
gaps.why: `confirmedBy: { message, matches }` asserts agreement. SSDP's removal signal is the opposite: NOTIFY * HTTP/1.1 with NTS: ssdp:byebye carrying a USN, which RETRACTS the presumed-alive fact immediately, before max-age expires. There is no expressible link from an inbound unsolicited message to the destruction of a fact created by a different message.
gaps.proposedFix: "invalidatedBy": [ { "message":"notifyByebye", "matches":"capture.hdrs | key('usn') == state.usn", "effect":"revoke" }, { "epoch":"bootId", "effect":"revokeScope" } ]  // symmetric with confirmedBy, same matcher grammar, no new expression machinery.

gaps.what: No unsolicited-inbound mode. §4 is send->expect shaped; SSDP's normal operating mode is a bare listener with no preceding request.
gaps.why: Devices multicast NOTIFY ssdp:alive on startup and periodically (before max-age lapses), ssdp:byebye on shutdown, and ssdp:update on a bootId change — none of them answers anything. A control point that only ever does M-SEARCH misses every arrival and every departure. `validIn` / `requires` / `conflicts` all presuppose you initiate the message; there is no state in which an unsolicited NOTIFY is legal or illegal, it simply arrives. Separately, acting as a responder means a 200 OK is legal ONLY within MX seconds of a matching received M-SEARCH — a legality rule keyed on an inbound message plus a timer.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a role axis to model: "roles": ["searcher","responder"], per-message "inboundOnly": true / "validAfterInbound": { "message":"mSearch", "withinMs":"capture.mx * 1000" }, and a step { "kind":"listen", "unsolicited": true, "on":"239.255.255.250:1900", "messages":["notifyAlive","notifyByebye","notifyUpdate"] } with no preceding send and no terminating edge.

gaps.what: No way to chain to a destination that came out of a capture — which is the only chain SSDP actually has.
gaps.why: Response bytes 99..139 are `http://192.168.1.42:49152/description.xml`. The mandated next operation is a TCP HTTP GET of that URL; everything useful about the device lives there. §5's `requires:["login"]` records that an earlier message succeeded, not that its capture supplies the next message's transport target. Nothing in v0 lets a layer's dst be an expression, so the chain crosses from expressible to not at exactly the point that matters.
gaps.proposedFix: Allow layer destinations to be expressions and add a `url` converter (Text -> Map with scheme/host/port/path): { "kind":"tcp", "dst": { "ip":"state.loc | url | key('host')", "port":"state.loc | url | key('port')" }, "frame": {"kind":"none"} } with the request-target taken from `state.loc | url | key('path')`. Same mechanism serves any redirect-style or endpoint-discovery protocol.

gaps.what: Case-insensitive header names plus variable optional whitespace make byte-exact re-encode impossible without preserving raw lexical form — and my own capture already violates the uniform template.
gaps.why: Response bytes 83..88 are `45 58 54 3a 0d 0a` — EXT, colon, CRLF. There is NO 0x20 after the colon and no value. A canonicalising writer emitting name + ": " + value produces 316 bytes, not 315, and the re-encode fails on a packet the decoder just read. Real devices compound this: `St:` / `Location:` / `usn:` mixed casing (all legal, all must match), multiple spaces after the colon, and obs-fold continuation lines. Any representation that normalises for lookup destroys the bytes; any representation that keeps bytes cannot do case-insensitive lookup.
gaps.proposedFix: The httpHeaders field kind stores each entry as { rawName, ows, value, index } and re-emits rawName + ':' + ows + value + CRLF verbatim in stored index order, while `key(name)` folds case for lookup. Encode-from-scratch uses a declared canonical form; encode-from-decode replays the raw form. This is the only fix that satisfies both §7.1 and §7.3 simultaneously.

gaps.what: No message-boundary declaration for a datagram. Nothing says the message ends at the blank line.
gaps.why: Response bytes 313..314 are the terminating 0d0a0d0a. §2's frame construct is explicitly 'declared once per connection' for stream framing; on UDP there is no connection and the frame is the datagram. If a device pads the datagram or (illegally but observably) appends a body, the parse has no defined stopping point and no way to assert that the remaining bytes are zero.
gaps.proposedFix: { "expect": "0d0a" } to consume the sentinel explicitly, plus { "assertEnd": true } (decode-only) which fails the parse if unconsumed bytes remain — or `{ "assertEnd": "lenient", "as": "trailing" }` to capture them. Cheaper and more precise than promoting `frame` to work per-message.

gaps.what: Step timeouts and listen windows are not expression-valued, and `timeout` is framed as a failure edge when here it is the success path.
gaps.why: MX (request byte 75) is a contract with the responders: each waits a uniform random 0..MX seconds before answering, so the collection window must be at least MX seconds plus network slack. The correct timeout is `mx * 1000 + slack` and no step field is documented as taking an expression, so it becomes a magic constant that silently desynchronises from the MX byte. And §4's edge vocabulary is ok|match|timeout|error|else — for a broadcast search, window expiry is the normal, successful completion of the operation, not an error condition. Absence of a reply is never evidence of absence in SSDP.
gaps.proposedFix: { "kind":"listen", "forMs": "inputs.mx | undecimal * 1000 + 500", "collect":"broadcast" } plus a distinct edge `"on":"window"` meaning 'the collection window closed normally' — leaving `timeout` to mean 'a reply we required did not arrive'.

gaps.what: No numeric bounds on injectable inputs, so a protocol-mandated range cannot be declared.
gaps.why: MX (byte 75) MUST be at least 1 and SHOULD NOT exceed 5; a device receiving MX greater than 5 treats it as 5, and a malformed or missing MX means the message is ignored entirely. §6 gives `type` values u8..u64 and `enum` but no min/max, so the constraint lives only in the prompt `description` — i.e. nowhere the engine can check.
gaps.proposedFix: { "name":"mx", "kind":"prompt", "type":"u8", "min":1, "max":5, "default":3, "description":"…" }, checked at input-binding time. Pairs with the `decimal` converter (gap 5) so the value can be both bounded and emitted as text.

gaps.what: Repeated header names and obs-fold continuation lines collapse under any single-valued representation.
gaps.why: HTTP permits a field name to appear more than once (combinable as a comma list), and permits a value to continue on a following line beginning with SP or HTAB. SSDP responses rarely do either, but vendor `X-` headers and GENA's `OPT` / `01-NLS` pairing do appear in the wild, and the parser must not lose or reorder them. A Text-valued map keyed by folded name silently discards the second occurrence.
gaps.proposedFix: Give httpHeaders multimap semantics: `key(n)` returns the first value, `all(n)` returns a List in wire order, and an obs-fold continuation is appended to the preceding entry's value while its raw bytes are retained in that entry's rawValue for verbatim re-emission.
